notes.note: Set A is better because it correctly extracts the specific geometry for the 'Roof Beam @ Grid 6 & Near Grid 5' (C1), identifying the 2'-6" spacing and 3" diameter openings, whereas Set B incorrectly attributes the 1'-3" spacing from beam B1 to this beam. Both sets share errors regarding the E6 beam label (reading 'D' instead of 'E6') and confuse E6 dimensions with B1 dimensions. Set A has fewer instances of mismatched dimensions to beam labels overall, particularly for the C1 beam layout.

Set B correctly identifies the 3-inch diameter openings for the roof beams (C1 and E6), whereas Set A incorrectly claims 8-inch or 6-inch rectangular openings for these members (e.g., claiming E6 has 8-inch openings). Set B also more accurately associates specific beam labels (B4, C4) with their sections, while Set A confuses Grid 2 (A4) and Grid 6 (A1) labels and dimensions. Both sets share some errors regarding the 6-inch opening width for Grid 6 (actual is 10-inch), but Set B's fidelity to the distinct roof beam details makes it superior.

Both sets contain identical significant errors: the first claim has a unit typo ('watt/ra'), and claims 2 and 3 misidentify the specific constant θ_K as the variable θ, supported by a misquoted string ('θ =' instead of 'θ_K ='). Both sets also include duplicate claims (2 and 3) and one correct claim (4). Set B's fourth claim has a slightly more descriptive attribute name, but this minor improvement does not outweigh the identical failures in the other three claims.

Both sets exhibit identical errors, specifically misreading the variable θk as θ in the graph's text box and hallucinating quotes that omit the 'k' subscript. Both sets also share a transcription typo in the first claim's unit ('watt/ra' instead of 'watt/rad'). The fourth claim in both sets is correct and faithful to the source text, making the overall quality equivalent.

Both sets extract the same four claims from Figure 7-3 and the surrounding text, with identical values, conditions and quotes. In both, the 6.302336º value is duplicated across two claims and mislabeled as generic θ rather than θK (the blade-pitch angle at which pitch sensitivity doubles), and both truncate the unit to 'watt/ra' in the first claim. Set B's fourth claim binds the property slightly more precisely (pitch sensitivity (∂P/∂θ) at θ = 0º) than A's, but this is a trivial wording difference and both are supported.

Both sets extract the same two figure values (∂P/∂θ at θ=0° = -25.52E+6 watt/rad and θK = 6.302336°) with supporting quotes, and both repeat the θK claim twice as a trivial duplicate. Both also truncate the unit in the first claim as 'watt/ra' instead of 'watt/rad'. The only difference is the fourth claim, where A binds the property as 'pitch sensitivity (∂P/∂θ) at θ = 0º' while B leaves it as generic 'pitch sensitivity' with the condition noted; both remain supported and neither invents anything.

Both sets contain identical claims with the same factual errors: Symbol 151 is incorrectly bound to Symbol 10's description (CU: #12/2WG), and Symbol 150 is incorrectly bound to Symbol 151's description (AL: Armored Cable). Set B uses the attribute 'conductor material' consistently for Wiring 150 whereas Set A uses 'material', but since the claims are factually wrong in both sets, the overall quality is equivalent.

Both sets contain identical critical errors, specifically misbinding Symbol 151's description to Symbol 150 and Symbol 10's description to Symbol 151 (e.g., claiming Wiring 151 is CU #12/2WG instead of AL Armored Cable). Set A is marginally more consistent in attribute naming ('conductor material' vs 'material' for Wiring 150), but this is negligible compared to the shared data binding failures.

The two sets are nearly identical in content and share the same errors: both misbind 'CU: #12/2WG.' (schedule symbol 10) to Wiring 151, misbind 'AL: 3#4/0, ARMORED CABLE' (symbol 151) to Wiring 150, and leave the 150 row's real spec (AL: 3#4/0, #4G., 2-1/2"C.) as a vague 'cable | specification' claim with no bound entity. The only substantive difference is that Set A labels the 150 claim's property as 'conductor material' while Set B uses the vaguer 'material'; A is marginally more precise and faithful. All other claims are equivalent, so A wins only narrowly.

The two sets are nearly identical in content and share the same errors: both misbind the '#12/2WG.' row (symbol 10/19) to Wiring 151, which is actually 'AL: 3#4/0, ARMORED CABLE', and both include a vague 'cable | specification' claim that duplicates the 150 entry without a proper entity. The only substantive difference is that Set B labels the 150 aluminum entry as 'conductor material' while Set A uses the looser 'material', making B marginally more precise and property-bound. Otherwise both correctly capture the CU/AL material, conductor size and conduit size for symbols 20, 31, 32, 33, 34, 50 and 150 with supporting quotes.
